edges.effect_quant: The most useful recent PCOS-specific meta-analysis found that anti-androgen regimens reduce hirsutism, and a one-year randomized trial showed larger hirsutism-score improvement with combined oral contraceptives plus spironolactone than with metformin alone. Older systematic review work in women with hirsutism also found spironolactone consistently better than placebo-level control for lowering Ferriman-Gallwey scores.
edges.population: women with polycystic ovary syndrome receiving spironolactone alone or as part of anti-androgen therapy
edges.mechanism: Spironolactone reduces hirsutism in PCOS by antagonizing androgen signaling at the hair follicle rather than by directly fixing the metabolic drivers of the syndrome. That makes it especially relevant for visible hyperandrogenic symptoms even when deeper ovulatory or insulin abnormalities persist.
edges.summary: Spironolactone appears effective for improving hirsutism in PCOS. The strongest modern evidence comes from anti-androgen meta-analysis and a randomized one-year PCOS trial, both of which support a clinically meaningful reduction in hirsutism scores rather than just a biochemical androgen change.
edges.caveats: Spironolactone is a symptom-directed anti-androgen, not a full PCOS disease-modifying therapy, and its use generally requires contraception because of teratogenic risk. The benefit is also gradual, so expectations should be set around months rather than weeks.

evidence.notes: Efficacy and safety of anti-androgens in the management of polycystic ovary syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
A systematic review of commonly used medical treatments for hirsutism in women.
